reference: GNU coreutils printenv, selected by PATH in the isolated reference Bash. Fixture variables are assigned and exported by the same script on both sides.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help metadata contracts
Exported scalar values with spaces and equals signs, empty values, and embedded newlines
No-operand environment listing includes an explicitly exported fixture entry
Unset and unexported names return failure without output
GNU option terminator, multiple operands, help, and invalid-option behavior
exclusions: The complete no-operand environment dump is not compared byte-for-byte because the runner deliberately gives reference and candidate Bash different PATH values; its case checks that a unique exported fixture entry is present.
No filesystem or privileged operations apply to this read-only command.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash resolves printenv as an enabled builtin, as required by the compiled-in loadable contract.
cases.script: type -t printenv

cases.purpose: Confirm the loadable's Bash help entry is registered and succeeds; the checked marker is independent of the external printenv CLI.
cases.script:
help printenv > metadata.out
printf 'help available\n'

cases.purpose: A named exported value containing spaces and an equals sign is printed exactly with one final newline.
cases.script:
VALUE='two words=three'
export VALUE
printenv VALUE

cases.purpose: An exported empty value is present and produces a single newline, rather than being treated as absent.
cases.script:
EMPTY_VALUE=
export EMPTY_VALUE
printenv EMPTY_VALUE

cases.purpose: An exported value containing an embedded newline is emitted byte-for-byte followed by printenv's terminating newline.
cases.script:
MULTILINE=$'first line\nsecond=value'
export MULTILINE
printenv MULTILINE

cases.purpose: With no operands, printenv lists the marked exported environment record; only this deterministic record is selected because the runner gives the two shells different PATH values.
A set but unexported shell variable and an unset name are both absent from the environment; the script captures each status and output before checking both behaviors.
cases.script:
LOCAL_ONLY=secret
unset PRINTENV_ABSENT
if output=$(printenv LOCAL_ONLY); then local_status=0; else local_status=$?; fi
if [[ -n $output ]]; then exit 2; fi
if output=$(printenv PRINTENV_ABSENT); then absent_status=0; else absent_status=$?; fi
if [[ -n $output ]]; then exit 2; fi
printf 'unexported=%s absent=%s\n' "$local_status" "$absent_status"
[[ $local_status -eq 1 && $absent_status -eq 1 ]]

cases.purpose: The standard -- option terminator permits a named variable operand after option parsing.
cases.script:
TERMINATED=after-options
export TERMINATED
printenv -- TERMINATED

cases.purpose: GNU printenv accepts multiple variable names and emits each value; the stock loadable source documents only one varname, so any incompatibility remains visible.
cases.script:
FIRST_VALUE=first
SECOND_VALUE=second
export FIRST_VALUE SECOND_VALUE
printenv FIRST_VALUE SECOND_VALUE

cases.purpose: GNU printenv queries environment names, so an exported Bash function is not found by its function name; this checks the loadable's function-specific branch against that behavior.
cases.script:
parity_function() { printf 'function body\n'; }
export -f parity_function
if printenv parity_function; then status=0; else status=$?; fi
exit "$status"

cases.purpose: Help succeeds and provides nonempty usage text. Branding and prose are implementation-specific.
cases.script: printenv --help > usage; [[ -s usage ]]; rm usage; printf "help available\n"

cases.purpose: An unsupported short option is rejected; GNU exit status is checked independently and diagnostic wording may differ.
cases.script:
if printenv -z; then status=0; else status=$?; fi
exit "$status"

cases.purpose: GNU printenv operand, exported environment, and option semantics.
cases.script: export A=first B=last; printenv A NOT_PRESENT B

cases.purpose: GNU printenv operand, exported environment, and option semantics.
cases.script: export A=first B=; printenv -0 A B

cases.purpose: GNU printenv operand, exported environment, and option semantics.
cases.script: export A=first B=last; printenv --null A B

cases.purpose: GNU printenv stops option parsing at the first variable; -0 here is an absent variable name.
cases.script: export A=first B=last; printenv A B -0

cases.purpose: GNU printenv operand, exported environment, and option semantics.
cases.script: export A=first; printenv A A

cases.purpose: GNU printenv operand, exported environment, and option semantics.
cases.script: A=temporary printenv A

cases.purpose: GNU printenv operand, exported environment, and option semantics.
cases.script: export POSIXLY_CORRECT=1 A=first; printenv A -0

cases.purpose: GNU printenv operand, exported environment, and option semantics.
cases.script: export A=first; printenv --nu A

cases.purpose: GNU printenv operand, exported environment, and option semantics.
cases.script: printenv --version > version; [[ -s version ]]; rm version; printf "version available\n"
